title: The 2.5D flip movie test agrees with the canvas on CI as it does on this Mac
goal: A check that a turning card exported to a movie looks the same as on the canvas failed on main in CI by a hair (776 off pixels against a limit of 768), turning main red. Find out whether the export really drifted (two recent commits changed which frame a time lands on) or the bar is too tight for compression, and fix whichever it is.
notes:
CI run https://github.com/dzearing/photonz/actions/runs/45074019141 (commit da5d5fad6), Test slice 2 of 3:
✘ Test "Three moments of a flip: the file's frame and the canvas's agree" recorded an issue at Space3DExportTests.swift:87:13: Expectation failed: (far → 776) < (pixels / 100 → 768)
Recent nearby commits: 924fa8d8e The frame shown at a whole second is the one that starts there; 959ef8eeb A new video keeps the length it was given. Filed by the runner of a-chart-or-title-keeps-what-you-set-by-hand-when, which does not touch export.
acceptance: The cause is named in the log: a real drift between file and canvas, or compression noise at the edge
Space3DExportTests passes on CI slice 2 and on this Mac

log.note: Failed again the same way on run 45076579800 (commit 8a40d9fdf, slice 1 of 3 this time): far 776 against 768. Exactly the same count twice suggests a steady drift rather than noise.

Cause: compression at the card's edge, not drift. Evidence: (1) CI's own log says every sampled frame landed exactly on its moment (400/700/1100ms) and the export picture equals the canvas pixel for pixel before encoding (pre-encode diff 0 here; CI's render-level 3D test reads 0 too). (2) Here, against canvas renders a frame early/late and 3/10ms off, the landed moment matches best every time (400ms: 287 far vs 3433/4566 a frame off). (3) Every far pixel here is within 1px of the card's edge (0 off-edge, hardware and software encoders alike); the 1px edge band is 1474-2076 pixels, so the old bar of pixels/100 = 768 was half the edge band, and CI's encoder fills more of it (776) than this Mac's (287). It was already at 741/768 on CI at 700ms before the frame-grid commit; that commit only moved which angles are sampled (397->400ms). Fix: the test now checks the frame starts at its moment, mean < 3, the landed moment beats the frame either side, and fewer than 0.1% of pixels are off more than 2px from the edge. Mutation (movie one frame late) fails all three moments on three checks.
